🧩 SATOM and the NAF Framework

Where SATOM sits in the Network Automation Forum's reference model: the source and its pinned commit, why SATOM aligns with it, what SATOM calls each block, and the conformance matrix that a test keeps honest.

SATOM and the NAF Framework

Audience: architects, auditors and integrators who need to place SATOM in a vendor-neutral reference model, and the team that keeps this mapping honest. The matrix in §6 is the only place the conformance state is recorded; every other document links here instead of repeating it.

Status line (generated from the matrix, checked by a test):

SATOM is conformant to the NAF Framework (commit da82b12): every MUST requirement is met.

1. Source, version pin and licence

  • Source: Network Automation Forum, The NAF Framework — https://reference.networkautomation.forum/Framework/Framework/
  • Repository: https://github.com/Network-Automation-Forum/reference, file docs/Framework/Framework.md.
  • Pinned commit: da82b12 (2026-04-28) — the last change to that file when this mapping was written. The framework carries no version number, so every SATOM surface that names it names this commit; a later rewrite of the framework cannot silently invalidate the matrix below. The release checklist (release pipeline) diffs the upstream file against the pin on every cut.
  • Licence: the reference repository is published under CC0 1.0. The diagram and the block icons on this page are reproduced from it unchanged (see NOTICE); their use follows the project's brand guidelines (block icon to the left of the block title).
  • There is no NAF certification. The conformance recorded here is a self-assessment against the pinned commit, checked by a test in this repository; the wording is conformant (self-assessed) or mapped to, never certified.

2. Why SATOM aligns with it

  1. Vendor-neutral and community-maintained. The framework is not a product's architecture rebranded as a standard.
  2. MUST / SHOULD / MAY makes conformance checkable. Each requirement is a sentence that is either met, partly met or not met — a matrix, not an opinion.
  3. A shared vocabulary. Customers, auditors and integrators who know the framework can read SATOM's architecture without learning SATOM's names first (§4 translates them).
  4. SATOM as one block in a customer's stack. A customer's NetBox can be the Intent block and their SIEM part of Observability; the framework's block boundaries are where SATOM plugs in.
  5. A yardstick for the roadmap. Every open row in §6 is a dated piece of work, and the status line at the top moves only when a row does.

3. The framework in one picture

The framework defines six functional blocks — Intent, Executor, Collector, Observability, Orchestrator and Presentation — "besides the actual network infrastructure" (its own wording). Infrastructure is drawn in the diagram and gets a row in the naming table, but it is the thing being automated, not a block of the automation system. Two cross-cutting expectations apply to every block: version control with CI/CD, and machine-friendly APIs documented by schema.

4. What SATOM calls each block

SATOM's names predate the mapping. This table is the translation; the product keeps its names (renaming "Source of Truth" would touch four language catalogs and dozens of pages for no functional gain), and the documentation says "in NAF terms this is …" where the two differ.

NAF block What SATOM calls it Read this when the names differ
Intent — desired state Templates, Template bindings, Baselines (template combos), the Exception Library, Change types, the secret vault SATOM calls the desired state Templates and Baselines; the NAF Framework calls this block Intent.
Observability — actual state, kept and processed Source of Truth (configuration history), Monitoring (the time-series store), the health engine and alerts, Drift, Sentinel, Scout, Release Advisor The main collision. SATOM's Source of Truth is the history of the actual configuration of each appliance. In NAF terms that is Observability, not Intent.
Collector — reading the network Device sync, Deep capture, Metrics collection (scrape targets), Log collection, the FortiAnalyzer log view satom-harvester is not the NAF Collector: it harvests vendor knowledge (API schemas, release notes), not network state.
Executor — writing the network The CLI writer, Policy operations and Clone, Provisioning, write actions, Firmware upgrade, Observatory fix The code calls a Process node's handler an "executor". That is a Process-engine term, not the NAF Executor.
Orchestrator — coordinating the blocks Processes (Studio), Scheduled Actions, Change Requests and the CR orchestrator, Integration hooks The SATOM reconciler is deployment and HA machinery (it brings a node to the released commit); it is not the NAF Orchestrator.
Presentation — people and other systems The web console, the satom CLI, API v1, the Documentation Center, notifications (bell, e-mail, webhook, syslog/CEF) —
Infrastructure — the network itself The managed appliances: FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiGate, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator Not a block of the automation system.

A second collision lives inside SATOM itself: "Baselines" names both the template combos of System provisioning (Intent) and Sentinel's behavioural baselines (Observability). The user guide says which one it means each time.

5. How to read the matrix

  • One row per requirement sentence of the framework, grouped by block, with the level the framework gives it (MUST, SHOULD, MAY) and two cross-cutting rows for the expectations that apply to every block.
  • Status is one of met, partial, gap, accepted-gap, n/a. An accepted-gap row states its reason after the dash: the requirement is understood and deliberately not pursued at this time.
  • Evidence is a file in this repository (a test checks that each one exists), so a rename cannot leave the matrix pointing at nothing.
  • The status line at the top of this page is derived from the matrix: the number of documented deviations is the number of MUST rows whose status is not met. A test fails when the sentence and the matrix disagree.
  • "Conformant" is a word the test owns. No published document may claim conformance with the framework while any MUST row is not met; when every MUST row is met, the status line changes and the word becomes available.

6. Conformance matrix — state at v3.4.0 (unreleased HEAD)

Block Level Requirement Status Evidence
Intent MUST Represent any network-related aspect in a structured form met app/models.py (Template, Baseline), app/models_tpl_binding.py, app/services/baselines.py
Intent MUST Create, read, update and delete the desired state met The console (app/views/templates.py, app/services/templates.py) and API v1 (app/api_v1/intent.py: templates, versions, bindings and baselines; versions are immutable, so an update is a new version, as in the console)
Intent MUST Expose that data through a standardized, documented API met app/api_v1/intent.py (read with scope read; write with the explicit template_draft / template_apply capabilities), documented in docs/api_v1.md §11–§12 and in the OpenAPI document of app/api_v1/openapi.py
Intent SHOULD Model in a neutral representation derived into vendor artefacts accepted-gap — SATOM is a Fortinet-specific product by design; app/services/template_compat.py translates between firmware builds, not between vendors app/services/template_compat.py
Intent SHOULD A unified view of the desired state across sources partial Templates and baselines are unified; IP addressing is delegated to NetBox through app/services/netbox_client.py
Intent SHOULD Governance metadata, validation, versioned access met app/services/templates.py (versions, approval, author, source firmware), app/services/template_compat.py
Intent MAY Rendering, decomposition and artefact generation met app/services/template_bindings.py (render), the dry-run → canary apply path
Executor MUST Interact with the supported write interfaces met REST clients in app/clients/, SSH in app/services/cli_writer.py (NETCONF and gNMI are not offered by the managed products)
Executor SHOULD Deploy full or partial configuration, reboots, software updates met Templates, app/services/policy_ops.py, the upgrade flow, app/services/provision_runner.py
Executor SHOULD Task input from the intended state or derived through Observability met Baselines and templates; app/services/observatory_fix.py applies from observed findings
Executor SHOULD Dry-run before executing met Every device write previews its diff first (app/services/fortiweb_ops.py)
Executor SHOULD Transactional execution met CLI sessions abort on the first error and re-read (app/services/cli_writer.py); REST writes are verified by app/services/device_verify.py
Executor MAY Imperative and declarative, idempotent operations partial Declarative templates (app/services/template_bindings.py) next to imperative actions; idempotence is not measured as a property
Collector MUST Retrieve live data over the read interfaces met REST clients, read-only SSH (app/services/ssh_ops.py), FortiAnalyzer JSON-RPC (app/services/faz_logs.py), app/services/metrics_collect.py
Collector MUST Extend beyond device APIs to SNMP, syslog, flow telemetry and packet capture met SNMP v2c polling per appliance (app/services/snmp_client.py, app/services/snmp_collect.py) and a syslog receiver in the scheduler sidecar (app/services/syslog_receiver.py), both under the satom_scrape_up contract; logs also arrive through FortiAnalyzer (app/services/faz_logs.py). Scope stated in docs/metrics-architecture.md: SNMPv3, traps, NetFlow/sFlow and packet capture are out of scope
Collector SHOULD Normalise values across vendors and methods partial Normalised across firmware builds and channels (app/services/api_library.py), single vendor by design
Observability MUST Persist historical data met app/services/sot_store.py (content-addressed configuration history), app/services/metrics_collect.py (time-series store), the audit log
Observability MUST Powerful programmatic access to that history met app/api_v1/observability.py: configuration history and diff per appliance over the Source of Truth, current findings, and a read-only MetricsQL query route over SATOM's own series (the time-series store itself stays on loopback)
Observability SHOULD A capable query language met MetricsQL dashboards (app/services/vm_store.py), internal to the console
Observability SHOULD Events when the actual state differs from the intended state met app/services/intent_compliance.py compares each bound device with its rendered template (key-subset diff); the Intent deviation check in app/services/alerts.py raises the finding and the typed hook event intent.deviation; Config drift (previous snapshot) remains a separate check
Observability MAY Enrichment with contextual and third-party information met app/services/release_advisor.py, app/services/drift_attribution.py, Sentinel (app/services/sentinel/)
Orchestrator MUST Coordinate processes across the blocks without touching the network directly met app/services/process_engine.py, app/services/cr_orchestrator.py
Orchestrator SHOULD Event-driven execution (synchronous, asynchronous, scheduled) met A Process declares a trigger event and filter; app/services/process_triggers.py starts the walk as a background job (never inside the scheduler tick), one running walk per process and device, rate-limited per process, rehearsal unless armed on trigger; hooks (app/services/integration_hooks.py), the console, Scheduled Actions and app/api_v1/processes.py are the other doors
Orchestrator SHOULD Reverse or compensating actions on error met The Compensate step in app/services/process_kinds.py undoes the walk's recorded steps newest first through each domain's own inverse (status flips, app/services/observatory_fix.py, app/services/provision_runner.py); a step without a recorded inverse is named unknown, never guessed
Orchestrator SHOULD Dry-run of a workflow met Unarmed Process runs (app/services/process_engine.py)
Orchestrator SHOULD Scheduled execution of a workflow met The run_process action in app/services/scheduled_actions.py walks a Process on any schedule (armed only when the action is armed and change-controlled)
Orchestrator SHOULD Logging and traceability of past and current workflows met app/models_process.py (ProcessRun, ProcessRunStep), app/models_cr_types.py, the audit log
Orchestrator MAY Correlate events and infer the course of action partial Cooldown and app/services/drift_attribution.py only
Presentation MUST Robust and flexible authentication and authorization met Local accounts with TOTP, LDAP and RADIUS (app/services/directory_auth.py), RBAC with ADOM scoping (app/services/access.py), owner-capped API tokens (app/models_api_token.py)
Presentation MAY Many forms: GUI, ITSM, messaging, documentation, dashboards met The console, NetBox and ticket integrations (app/services/change_requests.py), hooks, the Documentation Center (app/views/manual.py)
Cross-cutting SHOULD Version control and CI/CD for every component met Signed releases (docs/release-pipeline.md), the audit runner, the reconciler
Cross-cutting SHOULD Machine-friendly APIs documented via schema met app/api_v1/openapi.py builds an OpenAPI 3.0 document from the live routes at GET /api/v1/openapi.json; tests/test_api_v1_openapi.py fails on any undocumented route; docs/api_v1.md remains the prose manual

Infrastructure has no rows: the framework places no requirement on the network itself.

7. What the status line counts, and what remains partial

The status line counts no MUST rows that are not met: with release 3.4.0 every MUST requirement of the framework is met, and the test that owns the word now allows conformant. This is a self-assessment against the pinned commit — the Network Automation Forum issues no certification — and it is only as good as the matrix above, which is why every row names its evidence and a test checks the file exists.

Three rows are deliberately not met, all SHOULD or MAY:

  1. Intent — a neutral model derived into vendor artefacts (accepted-gap). SATOM is a Fortinet-specific product; its templates are the vendor's own objects. The row stays open on purpose.
  2. Intent — a unified view across sources and Collector — normalise across vendors (partial). Both are single-vendor by the same decision; IP addressing is delegated to NetBox rather than modelled twice.
  3. Executor — idempotent operations and Orchestrator — correlate events (partial). Idempotence is designed for but not measured as a property; correlation is limited to cooldowns and drift attribution.

Scope statements that keep the MUST rows honest: the Collector row is met by SNMP v2c polling and a syslog receiver — SNMPv3, traps, flow telemetry and packet capture are out of scope and docs/metrics-architecture.md says so; the Intent write API never writes to a device directly (a push is the console's own canary-gated job); the metrics query route is the only way to the time-series store from outside, which stays bound to loopback.

8. Keeping this page honest

  • One matrix. The Documentation Center article and every other manual link here; none repeats the status table.
  • A test owns the wording. tests/test_naf_alignment_doc.py parses the matrix, recomputes the number of deviations, checks that every evidence file exists, that the pinned commit and source URL are identical on every surface, that no document claims conformance while a MUST row is open, and that the release checklist still carries the upstream-diff item.
  • Update the matrix in the release that changes a row — not before (a claim without code) and not after (code without a claim).
  • Upstream drift. At every release cut, diff the upstream Framework.md against the pinned commit. If it changed, re-run the mapping and bump the pin on every surface. The check is a release-checklist step, never a network call inside a test.
